blocks.text: Microbiological pollution is the contamination of water by harmful microorganisms, such as bacteria, viruses, protozoa, and parasites which can pose serious health risks to humans and animals. This type of pollution typically results from the discharge of untreated or inadequately treated sewage, animal waste, hospital waste, and runoff from agricultural lands into water bodies. Common pathogens found in microbiologically polluted water include Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Giardia. Microorganisms in water, such as bacteria, viruses, and protozoa are the major cause of water-borne diseases. Common water-borne diseases include cholera, typhoid, dysentery, and hepatitis A.
